idiom_name: testify mock.Mock embedded in a stub + AssertCalled/AssertNumberOfCalls
implementation_notes: The dominant library realization embeds testify's mock.Mock in a test type: each method calls o.Called(args...) to record the invocation (and obtain canned returns), and the test asserts afterwards with o.AssertCalled(t, "Save", ...), AssertNumberOfCalls, AssertNotCalled or AssertExpectations. What replaces the classic spy object is this embedded recorder plus the assertion helpers; because Go interfaces are implicit, the double only has to satisfy the consumer interface, and a hand-rolled slice of recorded calls is the standard no-dependency alternative.
pitfalls: Called(...) records only when the double's method actually invokes it; a method that returns directly records nothing and the assertion fails confusingly.
AssertCalled compares with ObjectsAreEqual (reflect.DeepEqual by default), so arguments with unexported fields, times or functions can fail despite looking equal.
Embedding mock.Mock in a value (not pointer) receiver copies the recorder, so assertions inspect a different log than the SUT populated.
